entries.label_vi: Thể thao đóng vai trò quan trọng: sức khoẻ, đoàn kết, tự hào, hình mẫu, kỷ luật, hoạt động kinh tế
entries.claim: Sport brings people together and teaches shared values.
entries.because: Teams and fans from different backgrounds unite around a common cause, athletes become role models for discipline and effort, and sport encourages millions of people to be active.
entries.result: Sport strengthens communities and national pride.
entries.reuse_vi: Đề vai trò xã hội của thể thao.

entries.label_vi: Thể thao bị thổi phồng: thương mại hoá, lương quá cao, doping, bạo lực cổ động viên, chủ nghĩa dân tộc cực đoan; tiền có thể dùng cho y tế, giáo dục
entries.claim: Sport is sometimes given more attention and money than it deserves.
entries.because: Professional sport is driven by money, scandals such as doping and corruption damage its image, and fan violence and extreme nationalism can divide people, while public money spent on stadiums could fund hospitals or schools.
entries.result: Its importance to society is exaggerated.
entries.reuse_vi: Phản biện vai trò thể thao.

entries.label_vi: Thể thao giúp lối sống lành mạnh: giảm tim mạch, béo phì; tâm trạng tốt; thể thao đồng đội tạo thói quen và quan hệ
entries.claim: Regular sport lowers the risk of serious disease and improves mood.
entries.because: Exercise strengthens the heart, controls weight, reduces stress and improves sleep, and team sports give people friends and routines that make it easier to keep going.
entries.result: People who play sport are more likely to stay active for life.
entries.reuse_vi: Đề thể thao và lối sống lành mạnh.

entries.label_vi: Khuyến khích vận động: cơ sở thể thao miễn phí, làn xe đạp, thành phố dễ đi bộ, giờ thể dục ở trường, chương trình nơi làm việc, chiến dịch, hỗ trợ phí tập
entries.claim: Governments should make exercise easy, affordable and enjoyable.
entries.because: Free or cheap facilities, safe cycle lanes and walkable neighbourhoods, school physical education, workplace schemes and subsidised club fees remove the barriers of cost, time and safety.
entries.result: More people move more every day.
entries.reuse_vi: Đề khuyến khích tập thể dục.

entries.label_vi: Sự kiện thể thao: du khách chi tiêu (khách sạn, ăn uống, đi lại), việc làm, hạ tầng, hình ảnh thành phố; nhưng chi phí và 'voi trắng'
entries.claim: Major sports events bring visitors, jobs and investment to the host area.
entries.because: Fans and teams spend money on hotels, restaurants and transport, temporary and permanent jobs are created, and new stadiums, roads and rail links remain afterwards, although costs can be very high.
entries.result: Benefits are greatest when facilities are planned for lasting use.
entries.reuse_vi: Đề sự kiện thể thao và kinh tế.

entries.label_vi: Vận động viên đại học tạo doanh thu lớn, chịu chấn thương và thời gian tập luyện; học bổng chưa đủ; nhưng công bằng với sinh viên khác, quỹ cho môn nhỏ
entries.claim: College athletes generate large revenues but receive little in return.
entries.because: Universities and broadcasters earn millions from matches, while players train for many hours, risk injury and struggle to study, and a scholarship may not cover their real costs.
entries.result: A fair payment, with safeguards for education and smaller sports, would reward their work.
entries.reuse_vi: Đề trả lương vận động viên đại học.

entries.label_vi: Cơ sở thể thao tăng tham gia (gần, an toàn, giá rẻ), nhất là với trẻ và người nghèo; nhưng cần bảo trì, chương trình, văn hoá
entries.claim: Local sports facilities increase participation, especially among children and low-income families.
entries.because: A nearby, safe and affordable pitch, pool or gym removes obstacles of distance and cost, but facilities that are poorly maintained or have no programmes are rarely used.
entries.result: Investment improves health only when it is combined with activities and good management.
entries.reuse_vi: Đề đầu tư cơ sở thể thao.

entries.label_vi: Sự kiện thể thao quốc tế: tự hào dân tộc, truyền cảm hứng tập luyện, giao lưu văn hoá, du lịch; rủi ro: sân vận động bỏ không, nợ
entries.claim: International sporting events can inspire people and promote understanding between nations.
entries.because: They create national pride, encourage young people to take up sport, bring visitors and cultural exchange, although stadiums that are unused afterwards and heavy debts are real risks.
entries.result: Careful planning decides whether they are an investment or a waste.
entries.reuse_vi: Đề sự kiện thể thao quốc tế.

entries.label_vi: Lương vận động viên: sự nghiệp ngắn, rủi ro chấn thương, tài năng hiếm, tạo doanh thu; nhưng y tá, giáo viên lương thấp, hình mẫu
entries.claim: Top athletes are paid according to the revenue they create.
entries.because: Their careers are short, injury is a constant risk, rare talent attracts huge audiences and sponsorship, yet nurses and teachers who serve society earn far less.
entries.result: The market rewards entertainment more than public service, which many people find unfair.
entries.reuse_vi: Đề lương vận động viên.

entries.label_vi: Thể thao thanh thiếu niên: thể lực, đồng đội, kỷ luật, bạn bè, tự tin, tránh rắc rối; hạn chế: áp lực, chấn thương, chi phí, loại trừ người kém
entries.claim: Youth sports programmes build fitness and social skills.
entries.because: Regular training develops strength and coordination, while team play teaches cooperation, discipline and how to cope with winning and losing, and clubs give young people friends and positive role models.
entries.result: Pressure to win, injuries, cost and the exclusion of weaker players must be managed.
entries.reuse_vi: Đề thể thao thanh thiếu niên.

entries.text: A small-town football club, for example, can bring together neighbours of all ages who would otherwise never meet.
An office worker who plays football with friends every weekend, for example, gets regular exercise without having to force himself.
A city that builds safe cycle lanes, for example, makes it easy for workers to exercise on the way to the office.
A town that hosts a championship match, for example, may fill its hotels and restaurants for a whole weekend.
A student athlete who injures a knee in a televised match, for example, may lose both his place on the team and his scholarship.
A new public swimming pool in a poorer district, for example, can give hundreds of children a place to exercise that their families could not otherwise afford.
A shy teenager who joins a basketball team, for example, often gains confidence and makes friends.

entries.label_vi: Du lịch mang lại thu nhập, việc làm, ngoại tệ, hạ tầng và niềm tự hào văn hoá
entries.claim: Tourism brings income, jobs and foreign currency to the host country.
entries.because: Visitors spend money on hotels, food, transport and souvenirs, which supports many small businesses, and the roads, airports and services built for tourists also benefit residents.
entries.result: Local people gain pride in their culture and history.
entries.reuse_vi: Đề lợi ích của du lịch.

entries.label_vi: Hạn chế: theo mùa, phụ thuộc, quá tải, thương mại hoá văn hoá, hư hại môi trường, lợi nhuận chảy ra ngoài
entries.claim: Dependence on tourism makes an economy fragile and can damage the places visitors come to enjoy.
entries.because: Income rises and falls with the seasons and with events such as disease or recession, crowds strain water and roads, and much of the profit may go to foreign companies.
entries.result: A balanced economy is safer than reliance on one industry.
entries.reuse_vi: Mặt trái của du lịch, phụ thuộc một ngành.

entries.label_vi: Du lịch nông thôn: việc làm, thu nhập, giữ người trẻ ở lại, bảo tồn nghề thủ công; nhưng việc làm theo mùa lương thấp, giá tăng, ồn, mất lối sống truyền thống
entries.claim: Tourism can give rural communities a new source of income.
entries.because: Farm stays, guided walks and craft sales create jobs where few exist and encourage young people to stay, but the work is often seasonal and low-paid, prices for locals may rise, and outside investors may take the profits.
entries.result: Benefits are greatest when the community owns and controls the businesses.
entries.reuse_vi: Đề du lịch nông thôn.

entries.label_vi: Lễ hội thu hút du khách ngoài mùa cao điểm, tạo chi tiêu, quảng bá hình ảnh; nhưng tạm thời, đông đúc, phụ thuộc tổ chức
entries.claim: Festivals give visitors a clear reason to travel and to spend money.
entries.because: A well-known music, food or cultural festival attracts people from other regions and countries, often outside the main holiday season, and fills hotels, restaurants and shops.
entries.result: The area also gains publicity, although the effect lasts only as long as the festival is successful.
entries.reuse_vi: Đề lễ hội và du lịch.

entries.label_vi: Du lịch ở hệ sinh thái mong manh: nguồn quỹ bảo tồn, nâng nhận thức, việc làm giảm săn trộm; nhưng giẫm đạp, rác, quấy rầy động vật, loài ngoại lai
entries.claim: Tourism in fragile ecosystems can fund their protection but also damage them.
entries.because: Entrance fees and local jobs give people a reason to protect wildlife, yet trampling, litter, noise and introduced species can harm habitats that recover slowly.
entries.result: Strict limits on visitor numbers and behaviour are essential.
entries.reuse_vi: Đề du lịch ở hệ sinh thái mong manh.

entries.label_vi: Du lịch một mình: tự do, linh hoạt, gặp người bản địa, trưởng thành; chi phí cao hơn, an toàn, cô đơn
entries.claim: Solo travel offers freedom, flexibility and personal growth.
entries.because: Travellers choose their own route and pace, meet local people more easily and learn to solve problems alone, although costs, safety and loneliness need attention.
entries.result: Many return more confident and independent.
entries.reuse_vi: Đề du lịch một mình vs tour đoàn.

entries.label_vi: Tour đoàn: an toàn, tiện, chia chi phí, hướng dẫn viên giỏi, bạn mới; lịch trình cứng nhắc, ít thật
entries.claim: Group tours are convenient, safe and good value.
entries.because: Transport, hotels and guides are organised in advance, costs are shared and a knowledgeable guide explains the history of each place, although the schedule is fixed and contact with local life may be limited.
entries.result: They suit first-time travellers and those short of time.
entries.reuse_vi: Đề tour đoàn.

entries.label_vi: Giải pháp du lịch có trách nhiệm: hạn chế lượng khách, phí môi trường, hỗ trợ doanh nghiệp địa phương, quy định rác và nước, giáo dục du khách, chứng nhận lưu trú xanh
entries.claim: Governments should limit the impact of visitors and keep the benefits local.
entries.because: Visitor caps and environmental fees protect popular sites, rules on waste and water reduce pollution, and certification and loans for local businesses keep more income in the community.
entries.result: Tourism can continue to grow without destroying what visitors come to see.
entries.reuse_vi: Đề du lịch có trách nhiệm.

entries.label_vi: Du lịch vũ trụ: thúc đẩy công nghệ, truyền cảm hứng; nhưng chỉ người giàu, phát thải, rủi ro, tiền nên dùng cho vấn đề trên Trái Đất
entries.claim: Space tourism may drive new technology, but its benefits to humanity are uncertain.
entries.because: Competition between companies can lower the cost of rockets and inspire young people to study science, yet flights are affordable only to the very rich, release significant emissions and carry real risks.
entries.result: Public money is better spent on problems on Earth.
entries.reuse_vi: Đề du lịch vũ trụ.

entries.label_vi: Tàu hoả: ít phát thải, từ trung tâm đến trung tâm, thoải mái, cảnh đẹp; chậm, đắt, ít tuyến. Máy bay: nhanh, đường dài; phát thải, thủ tục sân bay
entries.claim: Trains suit short and medium journeys, while planes suit long distances.
entries.because: Trains produce far fewer emissions per passenger, run from city centre to city centre and offer comfort and scenery, whereas planes cut hours from long journeys but add airport queues and pollution.
entries.result: The best choice depends on distance, price and time.
entries.reuse_vi: Đề tàu vs máy bay.

entries.label_vi: Du lịch đại trà: thu nhập và việc làm lớn; nhưng rác, khí thải, dùng nước, phá môi trường sống; chỉ lợi hơn khi được quản lý
entries.claim: Mass tourism creates income for millions but can harm the environment on a large scale.
entries.because: Crowds produce litter, emissions and heavy water use, and coastlines and wildlife suffer, yet whole regions depend on the jobs that visitors provide.
entries.result: Benefits outweigh the damage only when numbers and building are controlled.
entries.reuse_vi: Đề du lịch đại trà.

entries.text: A family that opens a small guesthouse, for example, earns a living and also buys food and services from neighbours.
A small island that relies on tourism, for instance, can lose most of its income in a single year if flights are cancelled.
A village that offers farm stays, for example, can keep young people from leaving to find work in cities.
A lantern festival held in the quiet winter months, for example, can fill hotels that would otherwise be empty.
Divers who touch a coral reef, for example, can destroy in a moment what took decades to grow.
A solo traveller who changes plans to follow a local's recommendation, for example, may discover a village that no tour would visit.
A group visiting an ancient temple with a trained guide, for example, learns far more than someone reading a brief sign.
A famous trail that issues only a fixed number of daily permits, for example, stays in good condition while still welcoming visitors.
A traveller who takes a train between two capital cities four hours apart, for example, arrives in the centre, rested, without airport queues.
A resort built directly on a beach, for example, can damage dunes and turtle nests while employing hundreds of local people.

entries.label_vi: Giữ gìn pháp luật: công dân tuân thủ tự nguyện và hợp tác; nhà nước ban hành, điều tra, xét xử công bằng
entries.claim: A law is only as strong as the willingness of citizens to follow it.
entries.because: Most laws are obeyed voluntarily and police cannot watch everyone, but only the state can make fair laws, investigate crimes and punish offenders lawfully.
entries.result: Citizens and government each carry part of the responsibility.
entries.reuse_vi: Đề trách nhiệm thực thi pháp luật.

entries.text: A driver who stops at a red light on an empty road, for example, shows a respect for rules that no number of cameras could produce.

entries.label_vi: Nguyên nhân tội phạm đô thị: nghèo và bất bình đẳng, thất nghiệp, ẩn danh, băng nhóm và ma tuý, gia đình yếu, thiếu cơ hội
entries.claim: Crime in large cities is driven by inequality, unemployment and weak social ties.
entries.because: Where some people see wealth around them but have no job or prospects, and where neighbours do not know one another, gangs, drugs and theft become more attractive and harder to detect.
entries.result: Young people without opportunity are most at risk.
entries.reuse_vi: Đề nguyên nhân tội phạm.

entries.label_vi: Giải pháp: việc làm, giáo dục, chương trình thanh niên, cảnh sát cộng đồng, thiết kế đô thị (chiếu sáng), điều trị nghiện
entries.claim: Governments should tackle the causes of crime as well as punish offenders.
entries.because: Jobs, education and youth programmes give people a stake in society, better lighting and design make streets safer, and treatment for addiction reduces the crimes that feed it.
entries.result: Prevention is more lasting and cheaper than punishment alone.
entries.reuse_vi: Giải pháp giảm tội phạm.

entries.label_vi: Kiểm soát súng: ít súng ít vụ chết người, khó tiếp cận với người nguy hiểm; nhưng tội phạm kiếm súng bất hợp pháp, bối cảnh khác nhau
entries.claim: Stricter gun control makes violent crime less deadly.
entries.because: Fewer guns in circulation and checks on buyers make it harder for dangerous people to obtain weapons and reduce deaths in arguments and accidents, although determined criminals can still find illegal guns.
entries.result: The effect depends on enforcement and on border and market controls.
entries.reuse_vi: Đề kiểm soát súng.

entries.label_vi: Cảnh sát răn đe và phản ứng ngay; dịch vụ xã hội (việc làm, tâm thần, nhà ở) giải quyết nguyên nhân
entries.claim: Police respond to crime while social services help to prevent it.
entries.because: Officers deter offenders and protect victims at once, whereas jobs, mental health care, housing and youth services reduce the pressures that lead people to crime in the first place.
entries.result: A mixed budget gives both immediate safety and lasting results.
entries.reuse_vi: Đề chi cảnh sát vs dịch vụ xã hội.

entries.label_vi: Hình phạt nặng hơn: răn đe phụ thuộc xác suất bị bắt hơn mức nặng; nhà tù tốn kém, tái phạm; nhưng tội nghiêm trọng cần hình phạt mạnh
entries.claim: The certainty of being caught deters crime more than the severity of the sentence.
entries.because: Offenders rarely expect to be caught, so longer sentences have little effect, prisons are expensive and often teach new crimes, but serious offenders must be kept from harming others.
entries.result: More police, faster courts and rehabilitation may work better than heavier penalties.
entries.reuse_vi: Đề hình phạt nặng.

entries.label_vi: Án tử hình: hiệu quả răn đe chưa được chứng minh, sai sót không thể sửa, vi phạm nhân quyền; ủng hộ: công lý, an toàn
entries.claim: There is no clear evidence that the death penalty deters crime better than long imprisonment.
entries.because: Many serious crimes are committed in anger or without expecting capture, a wrongful execution cannot be reversed, and many people believe that the state should not take life.
entries.result: Supporters argue that it delivers justice and permanently protects society.
entries.reuse_vi: Đề án tử hình.

entries.label_vi: Trò chơi điện tử và bạo lực: bằng chứng yếu, đa số người chơi không bạo lực; nhưng có thể tăng hung hăng ngắn hạn, trẻ nhỏ, cần kiểm soát của cha mẹ
entries.claim: Evidence that video games cause real violence is weak.
entries.because: Hundreds of millions of people play violent games without harming anyone, and violent crime has fallen in several countries as gaming has grown, although games may increase aggression briefly and are unsuitable for young children.
entries.result: Family background and mental health matter far more.
entries.reuse_vi: Đề trò chơi điện tử và bạo lực.

entries.label_vi: Trộm danh tính: cá nhân dùng mật khẩu mạnh, cẩn thận; công ty và chính phủ cần luật, bảo mật, trừng phạt, bảo vệ dữ liệu
entries.claim: Preventing identity theft needs both careful individuals and strong protection from institutions.
entries.because: People can use strong passwords, avoid suspicious links and check statements, but only banks, companies and governments can secure stored data, pursue criminals across borders and set penalties.
entries.result: Neither side can solve the problem alone.
entries.reuse_vi: Đề trộm danh tính, an ninh mạng.

entries.label_vi: Nghèo và thiếu giáo dục tăng rủi ro tội phạm nhưng đa số người nghèo không phạm tội; trách nhiệm cá nhân vẫn quan trọng
entries.claim: Poverty and poor education raise the risk of crime, but they do not excuse it.
entries.because: People with no job and no prospects face stronger temptation and fewer legitimate options, yet most poor people obey the law, and crime also occurs among the wealthy.
entries.result: Both social conditions and personal choice must be addressed.
entries.reuse_vi: Đề nguyên nhân tội phạm: nghèo vs trách nhiệm.

entries.text: A teenager who leaves school with no qualifications and no job, for example, may be drawn by a gang that offers money and belonging.
An argument between neighbours, for example, is far less likely to end in a death if neither has easy access to a gun.
A thief who believes that he will probably not be caught, for example, is hardly influenced by whether the maximum sentence is five or ten years.
A man who is executed and later proved innocent, for example, cannot be given back his life.
A teenager who plays a shooting game with friends in the evening, for example, usually treats it as entertainment, as he would a film.
A person who receives an email that appears to come from the bank, for example, may give away passwords unless he or she has been warned about such tricks.

entries.label_vi: Luật giao thông chặt (giới hạn tốc độ, dây an toàn, cấm lái xe say, camera) giảm tai nạn; nhưng cần thực thi, thiết kế đường, an toàn xe, giáo dục
entries.claim: Stricter traffic laws save lives when they are enforced.
entries.because: Speed limits, seat-belt rules and drink-driving laws, backed by cameras and checks, change how people drive, but road design, vehicle safety and education also matter.
entries.result: Laws that are not enforced have little effect.
entries.reuse_vi: Đề luật giao thông và tai nạn.

entries.label_vi: Cấm trừng phạt thể xác: hại thể chất và tinh thần, dạy bạo lực, quyền trẻ em; phương pháp kỷ luật tích cực thay thế
entries.claim: Hitting children harms them and teaches them that violence solves problems.
entries.because: Physical punishment can cause injury, fear and anxiety, and children who are hit are more likely to be aggressive, whereas calm explanation and consistent consequences teach self-control.
entries.result: Children have the same right to protection from assault as adults.
entries.reuse_vi: Đề trừng phạt thể xác của cha mẹ.

entries.label_vi: Phản biện: luật khó thực thi trong gia đình, có thể hình sự hoá cha mẹ; nên giáo dục và hỗ trợ trước
entries.claim: A ban is hard to enforce in the privacy of the home.
entries.because: Many parents who slap a child are stressed rather than cruel, prosecuting them may harm the family further, and support and education usually work better than punishment.
entries.result: The law should set a clear standard but focus on help.
entries.reuse_vi: Giới hạn / nhượng bộ trong đề cấm đánh con.

entries.label_vi: Báo cáo sai phạm: cá nhân thường biết trước; nhưng sợ bị trả đũa; cần luật bảo vệ người tố giác và kênh an toàn
entries.claim: People inside an organisation often know about wrongdoing before anyone else.
entries.because: Colleagues see fraud, abuse or unsafe practices first, but fear of losing their job or being punished stops many from speaking, so legal protection and safe reporting channels are needed.
entries.result: Reporting works only when it is safe.
entries.reuse_vi: Đề báo cáo sai phạm, tham nhũng.

entries.label_vi: Minh bạch: công khai hợp đồng, ngân sách, cơ quan chống tham nhũng độc lập, kiểm toán, phương tiện truyền thông tự do
entries.claim: Governments must make public spending transparent.
entries.because: Open contracts, published budgets, independent audits and a free press make it harder to hide corruption, and independent agencies can investigate without fear of the people they examine.
entries.result: Citizens' reports are then more likely to lead to action.
entries.reuse_vi: Đề tham nhũng, minh bạch.

entries.label_vi: Cảnh sát cộng đồng: quen cư dân, hiểu địa phương, thông tin sớm, tin tưởng, ngăn tội phạm; nhưng cần nhân lực, không phù hợp mọi nơi
entries.claim: Community policing builds trust between officers and residents.
entries.because: Officers who walk the same streets, meet shopkeepers and talk to young people learn about local problems early, and residents who trust them are more willing to share information.
entries.result: Crime is prevented and solved more often, though it needs more officers and may not suit every area.
entries.reuse_vi: Đề cảnh sát cộng đồng.

entries.label_vi: Câu lạc bộ thanh niên: chỗ an toàn, hoạt động tích cực, người hướng dẫn, kỹ năng; giảm tội phạm; hạn chế: không đến được nhóm nguy cơ, kinh phí
entries.claim: Youth clubs give young people safe places, positive activities and role models.
entries.because: Sport, music and mentoring fill the unsupervised hours when many offences occur, teach teamwork and skills, and give young people a sense of belonging that gangs might otherwise provide.
entries.result: They reduce crime only if they reach those most at risk and are properly funded.
entries.reuse_vi: Đề câu lạc bộ thanh niên và tội phạm.

entries.label_vi: Đầu tư thực thi pháp luật: cảnh sát được đào tạo, công nghệ điều tra, toà án nhanh hơn; phối hợp với phòng ngừa
entries.claim: A well-funded law enforcement system catches more offenders and delivers justice faster.
entries.because: Trained detectives, modern forensic technology and enough judges reduce backlogs, so that victims see results and offenders expect to be caught.
entries.result: Investment should be balanced with prevention and fair treatment.
entries.reuse_vi: Đề đầu tư luật pháp, toà án.

entries.text: A stretch of road with speed cameras, for example, often sees far fewer serious crashes because drivers slow down.
A child who is smacked for shouting, for example, may learn that adults solve problems by hitting, and may copy that behaviour at school.
An accountant who notices false invoices at her firm, for example, may stay silent for fear of losing her job.
A city that publishes every building contract online, for example, allows journalists and citizens to spot suspicious prices.
An officer who walks the same neighbourhood every day, for example, may learn about a bullying problem from a shopkeeper before it becomes serious.
A youth club that opens until ten at night, for example, gives teenagers somewhere to go instead of wandering the streets.
A victim who must wait three years for a trial, for example, may lose faith in the justice system.

entries.label_vi: Internet cho mọi người tiếng nói không cần người gác cổng; hỗ trợ người bất đồng chính kiến; nhưng tin giả, quấy rối, chính phủ chặn và theo dõi
entries.claim: The internet gives ordinary people a platform that no one controls.
entries.because: Anyone with a connection can publish opinions, share news and organise with others without needing a newspaper or broadcaster, which helps those whose views are ignored or suppressed.
entries.result: The same freedom allows rumour, harassment and surveillance by governments.
entries.reuse_vi: Đề internet và tự do ngôn luận.

entries.label_vi: Kiểm duyệt: khó hiệu quả (dễ lách), tốn tiền, che giấu sự thật, giảm niềm tin; nhưng nội dung cực hại (lạm dụng trẻ em, kích động) cần hạn chế
entries.claim: Broad censorship wastes money and rarely achieves its aim.
entries.because: Determined people find ways around blocks, officials must spend large sums on monitoring, and hiding information damages public trust, although a narrow set of content such as child abuse and direct incitement to violence justifies control.
entries.result: Targeted rules are more defensible than general censorship.
entries.reuse_vi: Đề kiểm duyệt.

entries.label_vi: Ngôn luận thù ghét trực tuyến: gây hại, kích động bạo lực, nền tảng tự điều chỉnh không đủ; nhưng nguy cơ hạn chế tự do, định nghĩa mơ hồ
entries.claim: Online hate speech causes real harm and should be limited by law.
entries.because: Abuse aimed at a person's race, religion or identity can drive victims offline, spread fear and sometimes lead to violence, and companies that profit from engagement cannot be left to regulate themselves.
entries.result: Rules must be narrow and clearly defined, with oversight by courts, to protect legitimate debate.
entries.reuse_vi: Đề kiểm soát ngôn luận thù ghét.

entries.label_vi: Mạng xã hội tăng hiểu biết chính trị: tin nhanh, dễ chia sẻ, thu hút người trẻ; nhưng buồng vang, tin giả, tham gia hời hợt
entries.claim: Social media makes political information faster, cheaper and easier to share.
entries.because: News, debates and campaign messages reach young people who rarely read newspapers, and ordinary citizens can question politicians directly, but echo chambers, false stories and shallow engagement limit the benefit.
entries.result: Awareness grows, but not always understanding.
entries.reuse_vi: Đề mạng xã hội và chính trị.

entries.label_vi: Công nghệ ảnh hưởng bỏ phiếu: quảng cáo nhắm đích, thông tin trên mạng, đăng ký trực tuyến, tin giả và bot; nhưng cũng giúp cử tri tìm hiểu
entries.claim: Technology shapes how voters learn about candidates and decide.
entries.because: Parties use data to target messages at individuals, social media spreads both information and false stories, and online tools make registration and research easier.
entries.result: Voters need skills to judge sources, and rules should make campaigning transparent.
entries.reuse_vi: Đề công nghệ và hành vi bỏ phiếu.

entries.label_vi: Truyền thông ảnh hưởng dư luận trong bầu cử: đặt chương trình nghị sự, cách đóng khung, hình ảnh ứng viên, 'cuộc đua ngựa', thiên vị; cần đa dạng và kiểm chứng
entries.claim: Media coverage decides which issues voters think about and how they see candidates.
entries.because: By choosing what to report, how to frame it and whom to interview, newspapers and broadcasters shape priorities, and a focus on personality and opinion polls can crowd out policy.
entries.result: A diverse media and independent fact-checking help voters to form their own views.
entries.reuse_vi: Đề truyền thông và bầu cử.

entries.label_vi: Bắt buộc bỏ phiếu: tăng tỷ lệ tham gia, đại diện hơn; nhưng hạn chế tự do, phiếu thiếu hiểu biết, bực bội; nên làm bỏ phiếu dễ dàng
entries.claim: Compelling people to vote treats a right as a duty and may produce uninformed choices.
entries.because: Citizens who are forced to attend a polling station may vote randomly or leave the paper blank, resent the state and lose the sense that voting is a free expression of opinion.
entries.result: Making voting easy and meaningful raises turnout without compulsion.
entries.reuse_vi: Đề bỏ phiếu bắt buộc.

entries.label_vi: Dễ bỏ phiếu: thêm điểm bỏ phiếu, bỏ phiếu sớm, bưu điện, trực tuyến an toàn, ngày nghỉ, hỗ trợ người già và khuyết tật, tự động đăng ký, thông tin nhiều ngôn ngữ
entries.claim: Governments should remove the practical obstacles that stop people from voting.
entries.because: More polling stations, early and postal voting, weekend or holiday elections, transport for older and disabled voters and automatic registration make it easier to take part.
entries.result: Turnout rises among workers, young people and minorities.
entries.reuse_vi: Đề làm bỏ phiếu dễ tiếp cận.

entries.label_vi: Nguyên nhân tỷ lệ cử tri thấp: thờ ơ, mất lòng tin, cảm giác phiếu không có giá trị, bất tiện (đăng ký, xếp hàng, giờ làm), thiếu giáo dục công dân
entries.claim: Low turnout reflects distrust, a feeling that votes do not matter and practical obstacles.
entries.because: Voters who believe that politicians are all the same or that the result will not change their lives see little point in taking part, and registration rules, long queues and working hours make voting inconvenient.
entries.result: Young and poorer citizens are the least likely to vote, so their interests are underrepresented.
entries.reuse_vi: Đề nguyên nhân bỏ phiếu thấp.

entries.text: A blogger who posts photographs of illegal logging, for example, can reach thousands of people even if the local newspaper stays silent.
A blocked website, for example, is often accessible again within hours through a different address or a virtual private network.
A woman who receives hundreds of abusive messages about her religion, for example, may stop speaking in public altogether.
A student who sees a politician's speech shared by friends, for example, may follow the story further, although she may also see only views that she already agrees with.
A voter who receives advertisements aimed at his age, job and neighbourhood, for example, sees a very different campaign from his neighbour.
A headline that announces which candidate is ahead, for example, can encourage some voters to follow the winner and others to stay at home.
A person who dislikes every candidate but must still go to the polling station, for example, may simply tick a name at random.
A nurse who works night shifts, for example, can vote during a week of early voting instead of missing the single election day.
A worker who sees a queue of two hours outside the polling station, for example, may decide that his time is better spent elsewhere.

entries.label_vi: Dịch vụ khẩn cấp cứu mạng ngay: cứu hoả, cứu thương, cảnh sát; sự cố vẫn xảy ra dù phòng ngừa tốt
entries.claim: Emergency services save lives at the moment when everything else has failed.
entries.because: Fire crews, ambulances and rescue teams reach people in danger within minutes, and some accidents and disasters happen however much prevention is in place.
entries.result: Cutting them would put lives at immediate risk.
entries.reuse_vi: Đề chi cho cứu hộ / khẩn cấp vs phòng ngừa.

entries.label_vi: Phòng ngừa rẻ và lâu dài hơn: giáo dục an toàn, quy chuẩn xây dựng, đê điều, y tế; ngăn thương vong từ đầu
entries.claim: Prevention stops harm before it happens and costs far less than repairing damage.
entries.because: Safety education, building standards, flood defences and health programmes reduce the number of emergencies in the first place, and the savings continue year after year.
entries.result: A balanced budget gives both immediate protection and long-term security.
entries.reuse_vi: Đề phòng ngừa vs khẩn cấp.

entries.label_vi: Chuẩn bị thiên tai: cứu mạng, giảm thiệt hại kinh tế, phục hồi nhanh, tăng niềm tin công chúng
entries.claim: Preparing for disasters saves lives and reduces economic damage.
entries.because: Early warning systems, evacuation plans, strict building codes and stored supplies mean that fewer people are hurt and communities recover faster.
entries.result: Every unit of money spent on preparation saves many times as much on repair.
entries.reuse_vi: Đề chuẩn bị ứng phó thiên tai.

entries.label_vi: Nguyên nhân tham nhũng: lương thấp, quyền lực không kiểm soát, thiếu minh bạch, hình phạt yếu, văn hoá dung thứ
entries.claim: Corruption grows where power is unchecked and punishment is weak.
entries.because: Officials with low pay and wide discretion are tempted by bribes, secrecy hides wrongdoing, and a culture that tolerates favours makes it seem normal.
entries.result: Public money is wasted and trust in government falls.
entries.reuse_vi: Đề nguyên nhân tham nhũng.

entries.label_vi: Giải pháp: minh bạch, cơ quan chống tham nhũng độc lập, bảo vệ người tố giác, lương đủ sống, hình phạt chắc chắn, giáo dục
entries.claim: Transparency, independent oversight and certain punishment reduce corruption.
entries.because: Open contracts and audits expose abuse, independent agencies investigate without fear, fair salaries reduce temptation, and protected whistleblowers make reporting safe.
entries.result: Public money is spent on its purpose and trust recovers.
entries.reuse_vi: Giải pháp chống tham nhũng.

entries.label_vi: Biểu tình là phần thiết yếu của dân chủ: tiếng nói ngoài bầu cử, gây áp lực, thay đổi lịch sử; nhưng gây gián đoạn, bạo lực, có kênh khác
entries.claim: Peaceful protest lets citizens speak between elections.
entries.because: Marches and demonstrations show politicians how strongly people feel, have helped to win rights such as votes for women and civil rights, and give a voice to groups that are ignored.
entries.result: Disruption or violence, however, can turn public opinion against a cause.
entries.reuse_vi: Đề biểu tình, dân chủ.

entries.label_vi: Hoạt động của thanh niên: năng lượng, ý tưởng mới, lợi ích dài hạn (khí hậu); nhưng thiếu kinh nghiệm, hoạt động hời hợt trên mạng
entries.claim: Young people bring energy, fresh ideas and a long-term stake to social change.
entries.because: They will live with the consequences of today's decisions on climate, housing and jobs, they are skilled at using social media, and they often challenge habits that older generations accept.
entries.result: Their impact grows when they work with institutions and sustain their efforts.
entries.reuse_vi: Đề hoạt động thanh niên.

entries.label_vi: Di cư có lợi cho nước nhận: lấp thiếu lao động, đóng thuế, kỹ năng, đa dạng, dân số già; thách thức: dịch vụ, hoà nhập, lương
entries.claim: Migrants fill gaps in the workforce and contribute to the economy.
entries.because: They work in hospitals, farms, construction and technology where employers cannot find enough staff, pay taxes, start businesses and help ageing countries to keep their workforce, although housing, schools and integration need planning.
entries.result: Benefits are greatest when newcomers are helped to learn the language and find suitable work.
entries.reuse_vi: Đề di cư.

entries.label_vi: Chính sách ngôn ngữ và thống nhất quốc gia: ngôn ngữ chung giúp giao tiếp, việc làm, giáo dục; ép buộc làm mất ngôn ngữ thiểu số, bực bội; chính sách đa ngôn ngữ
entries.claim: A shared language can unite a country, but forcing it can divide.
entries.because: A common language gives everyone access to education, jobs and public services, yet suppressing minority languages makes people feel that their identity is threatened.
entries.result: Policies that promote a national language while respecting others are more likely to build unity.
entries.reuse_vi: Đề chính sách ngôn ngữ.

entries.label_vi: Nghĩa vụ quân sự: kỷ luật, kỹ năng, hoà nhập xã hội, phòng thủ; nhưng mất học tập và nghề nghiệp, cưỡng ép, chi phí, quân đội chuyên nghiệp hơn
entries.claim: Compulsory service can teach discipline and bring citizens from different backgrounds together.
entries.because: Recruits learn teamwork, fitness and practical skills and meet people they would never otherwise meet, but they lose time for study and work, and many countries find professional forces more effective.
entries.result: The benefits depend on how well the programme is designed and whether alternatives are offered.
entries.reuse_vi: Đề nghĩa vụ quân sự / dân sự.

entries.label_vi: Nghĩa vụ quốc gia (dân sự hoặc quân sự) tăng trách nhiệm công dân: phục vụ cộng đồng, hiểu xã hội, đóng góp; cần lựa chọn và ý nghĩa
entries.claim: National service can strengthen civic responsibility if it is meaningful.
entries.because: Young people who spend a year helping in hospitals, schools or emergency teams see the needs of their community, learn to cooperate and often keep volunteering afterwards.
entries.result: Pointless or forced tasks may create resentment instead.
entries.reuse_vi: Đề nghĩa vụ quốc gia và trách nhiệm công dân.

entries.text: A person who suffers a heart attack, for example, may survive only if an ambulance arrives within minutes.
A town that builds flood walls and drains, for example, may avoid damage that would cost far more to repair after every storm.
A country in an earthquake zone that enforces strict building codes, for example, loses far fewer lives than one that does not.
An official who is paid very little and controls permits, for example, may be tempted to ask for a bribe to approve an application.
A peaceful march of thousands of people through the capital, for example, shows politicians that an issue cannot be ignored.
Students who leave lessons to demand action on climate change, for example, can put the issue on the front page of newspapers.
A hospital that depends on nurses from abroad, for example, would struggle to keep its wards open without them.
A region whose road signs and schools use both the national and the local language, for example, lets residents feel that their culture is respected.
A recruit from a farming village sharing a barracks with a student from the capital, for example, learns about a very different way of life.
A school leaver who spends a year helping in a care home, for example, may continue to volunteer for years afterwards.

entries.label_vi: Công nghệ và quan hệ: giữ liên lạc xa, tạo quan hệ mới; nhưng giảm thời gian gặp mặt, điện thoại ở bàn ăn, giao tiếp hời hợt, bắt nạt mạng
entries.claim: Technology helps people to stay in touch but can weaken the quality of time together.
entries.because: Video calls and messages connect families and friends across distances, yet phones at the dinner table, constant notifications and online bullying reduce attention and can make contact shallow.
entries.result: Relationships benefit when technology is used to add to, not replace, face-to-face contact.
entries.reuse_vi: Đề công nghệ và quan hệ.

entries.label_vi: Tình nguyện: lấp khoảng trống dịch vụ, xây cộng đồng; người làm được kỹ năng, ý nghĩa, bạn bè
entries.claim: Volunteering benefits both the community and the volunteer.
entries.because: Volunteers provide help that public services cannot always afford, from tutoring to care for older people, while they gain skills, friendships and a sense of purpose.
entries.result: Neither side benefits alone, and the effect is greatest when the work is well organised.
entries.reuse_vi: Đề tình nguyện.

entries.label_vi: Tình nguyện ở nước ngoài: cộng đồng có thêm nhân lực, kỹ năng; tình nguyện viên hiểu văn hoá; nhưng ngắn hạn, phụ thuộc, 'du lịch tình nguyện'
entries.claim: Volunteering abroad can help communities if it matches local needs.
entries.because: Volunteers with skills such as teaching or medicine fill real gaps and learn about other cultures, yet short, poorly planned visits may take work from local people and create dependence.
entries.result: Projects led by the community give the most lasting benefit.
entries.reuse_vi: Đề tình nguyện viên ở nước ngoài.

entries.label_vi: Tình nguyện: lựa chọn cá nhân và động lực; chính phủ khuyến khích (điểm ở trường, nghỉ phép, ưu đãi thuế, hạ tầng)
entries.claim: Volunteering depends on personal motivation but is helped by public encouragement.
entries.because: People volunteer when they care about a cause, yet schools, employers and governments can make it easier through course credit, paid time off, recognition and well-run organisations.
entries.result: A mixture of personal choice and public support gives the best results.
entries.reuse_vi: Đề cá nhân vs chính phủ khuyến khích tình nguyện.

entries.label_vi: Thú cưng: bầu bạn, giảm cô đơn, niềm vui; nhưng không bằng thành viên gia đình (trách nhiệm đạo đức, quan hệ, thừa kế)
entries.claim: Pets give companionship and joy but cannot replace human family members.
entries.because: They reduce loneliness and encourage exercise and responsibility, yet they cannot offer the shared history, conversation and mutual obligations that bind a family.
entries.result: Pets are important to many people without being equal to relatives.
entries.reuse_vi: Đề thú cưng.

entries.label_vi: Nguyên nhân sinh thấp: chi phí nuôi con, nhà ở đắt, phụ nữ học cao và đi làm, kết hôn muộn, khó cân bằng công việc, bất ổn
entries.claim: Low birth rates reflect the high cost of raising children and the difficulty of combining work and family.
entries.because: Housing, childcare and education are expensive, women increasingly pursue careers and marry later, and long working hours and insecure jobs make couples delay or limit families.
entries.result: Many people end up with fewer children than they would like.
entries.reuse_vi: Đề sinh suất thấp.

entries.label_vi: Giải pháp: chăm sóc trẻ giá phải chăng, hỗ trợ nhà ở, nghỉ thai sản cho cả hai, giờ làm linh hoạt, hỗ trợ tài chính
entries.claim: Governments should make it easier for couples to have the children they want.
entries.because: Affordable childcare, housing support, parental leave for both parents, flexible working and financial help reduce the costs and career penalties of having a child.
entries.result: Families can have children without sacrificing security or careers.
entries.reuse_vi: Giải pháp sinh suất thấp, chính sách thân thiện gia đình.

entries.label_vi: Chăm sóc trẻ nhỏ: phát triển não, sẵn sàng đi học, cha mẹ đi làm, bình đẳng, lợi ích dài hạn
entries.claim: Good care in the early years gives children a lasting advantage.
entries.because: The brain develops fastest before the age of five, and quality nurseries build language, social skills and curiosity while allowing parents, especially mothers, to work.
entries.result: Children arrive at school ready to learn, and the country gains healthier, more productive citizens.
entries.reuse_vi: Đề chăm sóc trẻ nhỏ.

entries.label_vi: Chi cho chăm sóc trẻ (đầu tư tương lai, cha mẹ đi làm) hay người già (dân số già, phẩm giá, giảm gánh nặng người nhà)
entries.claim: Both children and older people depend on public care, but their needs differ in timing and urgency.
entries.because: Childcare invests in the future and lets parents work, whereas elder care protects the dignity of people who built the country and relieves relatives who often care at the expense of their jobs.
entries.result: A balanced budget that responds to demographic change is wise.
entries.reuse_vi: Đề chi chăm sóc trẻ vs người già.

entries.label_vi: Vai trò cha mẹ với thành tích học: động viên, nếp sinh hoạt, tài liệu, quan tâm, kỳ vọng hợp lý; quá áp lực phản tác dụng
entries.claim: Parents shape children's academic success through encouragement, routine and interest.
entries.because: Children whose parents read with them, set regular times for homework and show curiosity about school tend to achieve more, while excessive pressure can cause stress and lower motivation.
entries.result: Support works better than pressure.
entries.reuse_vi: Đề cha mẹ và học tập.

entries.label_vi: Hạn chế điện thoại thông minh cho trẻ: xao nhãng học, mất ngủ, bắt nạt mạng, nội dung không phù hợp, ít vận động; nhưng liên lạc an toàn và học tập
entries.claim: Young children are not ready for unrestricted smartphones.
entries.because: Phones distract from schoolwork, disturb sleep, expose children to unsuitable content and online bullying and replace play and exercise, although they allow parents and children to stay in contact.
entries.result: Delaying and limiting use protects health, learning and development.
entries.reuse_vi: Đề trẻ em dùng điện thoại, thời gian màn hình.

entries.label_vi: Ông bà: chăm cháu, truyền giá trị và câu chuyện, hỗ trợ cha mẹ đi làm, an toàn cảm xúc; khác biệt quan điểm nuôi dạy, sức khoẻ
entries.claim: Grandparents provide care, stability and a link with the past.
entries.because: They look after grandchildren while parents work, pass on stories, values and skills, and give children a sense of security, though their ideas about discipline may differ from the parents'.
entries.result: Children with close grandparents often feel more rooted and loved.
entries.reuse_vi: Đề ông bà.

entries.label_vi: Truyền thống gia đình: cảm giác thuộc về, giá trị, liên tục thế hệ; có thể gò bó
entries.claim: Family traditions give children a sense of belonging and identity.
entries.because: Shared rituals such as festival meals, stories and customs pass on values and memories from one generation to the next, although rigid traditions can limit individual choice.
entries.result: People with strong traditions often feel more secure about who they are.
entries.reuse_vi: Đề truyền thống gia đình và bản sắc.

entries.text: A grandmother who watches her grandchildren's school play by video call from another country, for example, feels part of their lives.
A retired teacher who helps children to read after school, for example, offers support that the school could not pay for and finds new purpose herself.
A volunteer who teaches English in a village for six months, for example, may help children but leave before the project can continue.
A widow whose dog greets her every day, for example, feels less alone, but the dog cannot replace the conversation of a relative.
A couple who postpone parenthood until they can afford a larger flat, for example, may find that they have only one child.
A child who spends mornings in a good nursery, for example, enters school already able to listen, share and speak in sentences.
A woman who looks after both her young children and her elderly mother, for example, may be forced to give up her job.
A parent who sits with a child for twenty minutes of homework every evening, for example, shows that learning matters.
A ten-year-old who scrolls on a phone in bed until midnight, for example, arrives at school tired and distracted.
A grandmother who tells stories about her childhood, for example, gives a child a living link with history.
A family that cooks the same festival dish together every year, for example, creates memories that tie generations together.
Smartphones, video calls and messaging apps

entries.label_vi: Hỗ trợ người già sống một mình: chăm sóc tại nhà, thăm hỏi, trung tâm cộng đồng, đi lại, báo động công nghệ, nhà ở phù hợp, hỗ trợ tài chính
entries.claim: Governments should help older people to stay safe, healthy and connected at home.
entries.because: Home-care services, regular visits, community centres, transport, alarm systems and suitable housing reduce risks and loneliness, and they allow people to live independently for longer.
entries.result: This costs less than residential care and respects older people's wishes.
entries.reuse_vi: Đề hỗ trợ người già sống một mình.

entries.label_vi: Hẹn hò trực tuyến: nhiều lựa chọn, tiện, giúp người nhút nhát hoặc bận, lọc theo sở thích
entries.claim: Online dating widens choice and makes it easier to meet compatible people.
entries.because: People can meet far more potential partners than in their daily circle, filter by interests and values, and begin conversations at their own pace, which helps the shy and busy.
entries.result: Many successful couples now meet online.
entries.reuse_vi: Đề hẹn hò trực tuyến.

entries.label_vi: Hẹn hò trực tuyến: lừa dối, hời hợt (đánh giá qua ảnh), quá nhiều lựa chọn khiến thiếu cam kết, an toàn, lừa đảo
entries.claim: Online dating can encourage deception and shallow judgements.
entries.because: Profiles can be exaggerated or false, people are judged quickly by photos, an endless supply of choices may reduce commitment, and some users face scams or safety risks.
entries.result: Careful use and meeting in public places reduce the risks.
entries.reuse_vi: Đề hẹn hò trực tuyến (mặt trái).

entries.label_vi: Bữa ăn gia đình: trò chuyện, ăn uống lành mạnh, cảm giác an toàn, ngôn ngữ, hành vi tốt hơn; khó vì lịch làm việc
entries.claim: Regular family meals support children's health, language and sense of security.
entries.because: Children who eat with their parents tend to eat more vegetables and less junk food, practise conversation and vocabulary, and feel that their lives matter to others.
entries.result: Busy schedules make the habit harder, but even a few shared meals a week help.
entries.reuse_vi: Đề bữa ăn gia đình.

entries.label_vi: Nuôi dạy nghiêm khắc: nếp rõ ràng, kỷ luật, an toàn, dự đoán được; nhưng sợ hãi, nổi loạn, ít sáng tạo
entries.claim: Clear rules give children structure, safety and self-discipline.
entries.because: When expectations and consequences are consistent, children know what to expect, learn to control impulses and are protected from risks, although harsh rules can cause fear, secrecy and rebellion.
entries.result: Rules work best when explained and applied fairly.
entries.reuse_vi: Đề nuôi dạy nghiêm khắc vs dễ dãi.

entries.label_vi: Nuôi dạy dễ dãi: tự do, sáng tạo, gần gũi, tự tin; nhưng thiếu ranh giới, khó tự chủ
entries.claim: A relaxed style encourages independence, creativity and close relationships.
entries.because: Children who are given freedom to make choices and are listened to tend to be confident and open with their parents, but without boundaries they may struggle with self-control and respect for others.
entries.result: A balance of warmth and limits is usually best.
entries.reuse_vi: Đề nuôi dạy dễ dãi.

entries.label_vi: Lễ hội cộng đồng: gặp gỡ, bản sắc chung, tôn vinh văn hoá, tình nguyện; nhưng ồn, loại trừ
entries.claim: Community festivals bring neighbours together and create shared memories.
entries.because: People who might not normally meet cook, perform and celebrate side by side, which builds trust, pride in the place and a sense of belonging.
entries.result: Festivals work best when everyone can take part.
entries.reuse_vi: Đề lễ hội cộng đồng gắn kết xã hội.

entries.label_vi: Chăm sóc trẻ do nhà nước tài trợ: cha mẹ (nhất là mẹ) đi làm, giáo dục sớm, bình đẳng, hoàn vốn; chi phí thuế, kiểm soát chất lượng
entries.claim: State-funded childcare pays for itself through higher employment and better child development.
entries.because: Parents, especially mothers, can work and pay taxes, children from poorer homes gain early education, and the economy benefits from a more skilled workforce, although the upfront cost and quality control need care.
entries.result: Benefits usually outweigh costs when the system is well designed.
entries.reuse_vi: Đề chăm sóc trẻ do nhà nước tài trợ.

entries.label_vi: Cha mẹ giới hạn thời gian màn hình: bảo vệ giấc ngủ, học, vận động, quan hệ; giới hạn cùng giải thích và làm gương
entries.claim: Parents should set sensible limits on screen time.
entries.because: Too much screen use reduces sleep, exercise and face-to-face play and can affect attention and mood, so clear limits protect development when combined with explanation and good example.
entries.result: Children also learn to manage technology for themselves.
entries.reuse_vi: Đề giới hạn màn hình.

entries.label_vi: Giải pháp: trợ cấp, thêm chỗ, đào tạo và lương người chăm trẻ, giờ làm linh hoạt, quy định chất lượng, hỗ trợ cộng đồng
entries.claim: Governments should make childcare more available, affordable and trustworthy.
entries.because: Subsidies, new places in nurseries, better training and pay for staff, flexible hours and clear quality standards reduce costs and give parents confidence.
entries.result: More parents can work without worrying about their children.
entries.reuse_vi: Đề chăm sóc trẻ giá phải chăng.

entries.label_vi: Nghỉ chăm con: khi cả cha và mẹ được nghỉ có lương, chia sẻ chăm sóc, giảm bất lợi nghề nghiệp của phụ nữ, bình đẳng; cần ưu đãi và giảm kỳ thị
entries.claim: Paid leave for both parents helps to share care and reduces career penalties for women.
entries.because: When only mothers take leave, employers may see women as less committed, whereas fathers who take time off become more involved at home and make childcare normal for both sexes.
entries.result: Equality improves when leave is well paid and fathers are encouraged to use it.
entries.reuse_vi: Đề nghỉ chăm con và bình đẳng giới.

entries.label_vi: Chính sách thân thiện gia đình: sinh suất, năng suất, bình đẳng, phúc lợi trẻ em, giữ chân nhân tài
entries.claim: Family-friendly policies benefit children, parents and the economy.
entries.because: Paid leave, flexible hours and childcare help couples to have the children they want, keep skilled workers in employment and give children a better start.
entries.result: Countries with such policies tend to have higher employment among women and stronger child wellbeing.
entries.reuse_vi: Đề chính sách thân thiện gia đình.

entries.label_vi: Lao động trẻ em: cá nhân (người tiêu dùng, cha mẹ) có vai trò; nhưng nguyên nhân là nghèo, cần luật, thanh tra, trường học, giảm nghèo
entries.claim: Child labour is mainly caused by poverty and can only be ended by action at several levels.
entries.because: Families that need income send children to work, consumers cannot always see how goods are made, and only governments can pass laws, inspect workplaces and provide schools and support for poor families.
entries.result: Individuals help by choosing ethical products, but the main responsibility lies with governments and companies.
entries.reuse_vi: Đề lao động trẻ em.

entries.label_vi: Cơ hội bình đẳng: cá nhân (thái độ, tuyển dụng công bằng); chính phủ (luật chống phân biệt, giáo dục, hỗ trợ nhóm thiệt thòi)
entries.claim: Equal opportunity needs fair attitudes from individuals and strong rules and support from government.
entries.because: Employers and neighbours can choose to treat people fairly, but discrimination is often hidden and structural, and only laws, public education and help for disadvantaged groups can change patterns that no single person controls.
entries.result: Both sides are necessary.
entries.reuse_vi: Đề cơ hội bình đẳng.

entries.text: An eighty-year-old who falls at home and cannot reach the telephone, for example, may lie for hours unless an alarm system calls for help.
A shy engineer who rarely meets new people at work, for example, may find a partner through an app that matches shared interests.
A child who talks about his day at the dinner table, for example, practises telling a story and feels that his parents are interested.
A teenager with a clear curfew, for example, knows what is expected and is less likely to stay out in unsafe places.
A street party where every household brings a dish, for example, lets neighbours who never spoke to each other become friends.
A mother who returns to work because nursery places are affordable, for example, pays taxes instead of receiving benefits.
A family that keeps phones out of bedrooms at night, for example, finds that children sleep better and arrive at school more alert.
A single parent who receives a subsidy for a registered childminder, for example, can take a full-time job instead of relying on benefits.
A father who takes three months of paid leave, for example, learns to care for a baby on his own and shares the load with his partner afterwards.
An employee who can start early and leave in time to collect her child from school, for example, stays in her job instead of resigning.
A ten-year-old who works in a brick factory to help his family, for example, misses school and may never escape poverty.
A company that removes names and photographs from applications, for example, can reduce bias at the first stage of hiring.

entries.label_vi: Nhà nước tài trợ nghệ thuật: thị trường bỏ qua nghệ thuật phi thương mại, mở rộng tiếp cận, giá trị văn hoá; nhưng thuế cho nhu cầu khác, nguy cơ kiểm soát
entries.claim: Public funding allows the arts to exist where the market alone would neglect them.
entries.because: Commercial success rewards popular entertainment, so experimental theatre, classical music and local museums often need grants to survive and to offer low prices, although governments should not control content.
entries.result: Society gains cultural diversity and wider access to the arts.
entries.reuse_vi: Đề nhà nước tài trợ nghệ thuật, trợ cấp công nghiệp văn hoá.

entries.label_vi: Chi cho khoa học (tăng trưởng, y tế, công nghệ) hay nghệ thuật (sáng tạo, bản sắc, sức khoẻ tinh thần); cần cân bằng
entries.claim: Science and the arts serve different but complementary needs.
entries.because: Science drives medicine, technology and economic growth, while the arts develop creativity, identity and wellbeing and often inspire scientific thinking.
entries.result: A balanced budget, with science receiving the larger share, serves society best.
entries.reuse_vi: Đề chi cho khoa học vs nghệ thuật.

entries.label_vi: Di sản: bản sắc, du lịch, không thể thay thế; hạ tầng: việc làm, nhu cầu hằng ngày, an toàn
entries.claim: Heritage cannot be replaced, but infrastructure meets daily needs.
entries.because: Historic buildings and traditions carry identity and attract visitors, and once lost they cannot be rebuilt, whereas roads, water and transport affect safety, jobs and living standards immediately.
entries.result: A mixed budget protects the irreplaceable while meeting urgent needs.
entries.reuse_vi: Đề di sản vs hạ tầng, trao đổi văn hoá vs hạ tầng.

entries.label_vi: Trợ cấp công nghiệp văn hoá: bảo vệ nhà sản xuất nhỏ trước cạnh tranh toàn cầu, việc làm, xuất khẩu, đa dạng; nhưng phụ thuộc, bóp méo
entries.claim: Subsidies can protect cultural industries from global competition.
entries.because: Small film, publishing and music sectors cannot match the budgets of international giants, and support lets local stories and languages survive while creating jobs and exports, though too much aid can reduce efficiency.
entries.result: Support should be targeted and temporary where possible.
entries.reuse_vi: Đề trợ cấp công nghiệp văn hoá.

entries.label_vi: Bảo tồn văn hoá: du lịch, bản sắc, giáo dục, gắn kết xã hội
entries.claim: Preserving culture gives a country identity, income and educational value.
entries.because: Historic sites, languages and traditions attract visitors, teach new generations about their roots and give communities a shared sense of belonging.
entries.result: Cultural preservation supports both pride and the economy.
entries.reuse_vi: Đề lợi ích của bảo tồn văn hoá.

entries.label_vi: Nghệ thuật và âm nhạc trong trường: sáng tạo, tập trung, tự tin, phát hiện tài năng, tiếp cận bình đẳng; nhưng thời gian, lựa chọn
entries.claim: Arts and music education develops creativity, discipline and confidence in every child.
entries.because: Learning an instrument or practising drawing trains concentration and patience, gives children a way to express feelings and may reveal talents that would otherwise remain hidden, and making it compulsory ensures access for pupils whose families cannot pay.
entries.result: The time it requires should not push out core subjects.
entries.reuse_vi: Đề môn nghệ thuật, âm nhạc bắt buộc.

entries.label_vi: Nghệ thuật hay khoa học quan trọng hơn: khoa học đáp ứng nhu cầu vật chất; nghệ thuật cho ý nghĩa, bản sắc; bổ sung nhau
entries.claim: Art and science meet different human needs, so neither is more important in every respect.
entries.because: Science improves health, safety and living standards, while art gives meaning, beauty and shared identity and shapes how people understand their lives.
entries.result: A society needs both.
entries.reuse_vi: Đề nghệ thuật vs khoa học.

entries.label_vi: Phục hồi toà nhà lịch sử vs xây mới: phục hồi giữ ký ức, bản sắc, du lịch, bền; xây mới đáp ứng nhu cầu hiện đại, chỗ ở, năng lượng; kết hợp tái sử dụng
entries.claim: Restoring historic buildings keeps identity, but new buildings meet modern needs.
entries.because: Old buildings carry memory, attract tourists and are often sturdy and well located, yet they can be costly to heat and adapt, and cities also need new homes and offices.
entries.result: Reusing historic buildings for modern purposes combines both aims.
entries.reuse_vi: Đề phục hồi vs xây mới.

entries.label_vi: Chi nghệ thuật hay thể thao: thể thao: sức khoẻ, hình mẫu, cộng đồng; nghệ thuật: sáng tạo, bản sắc, tinh thần; cả hai giá trị; cân bằng
entries.claim: Both arts and sport improve wellbeing, but in different ways.
entries.because: Sport improves physical health and builds teamwork and community pride, whereas the arts develop creativity, cultural identity and mental wellbeing, and both attract visitors and give young people a sense of purpose.
entries.result: A balanced budget gives every talent a chance.
entries.reuse_vi: Đề chi nghệ thuật vs thể thao.

entries.text: A small theatre that stages new plays, for example, may never make a profit but enriches the cultural life of a city.
An engineer who designs a bridge, for example, needs science to make it strong and art to make it beautiful.
A medieval bridge that is allowed to fall into the river, for example, can never be rebuilt, whereas a modern road can be repaired next year.
A small country that funds its own films, for example, can tell stories in its own language that foreign studios would never produce.
A well-preserved old town, for example, can draw visitors from around the world and support hundreds of local jobs.
A shy pupil who joins the school choir, for example, may discover a talent and gain confidence that she would never have found in maths class.
An old factory converted into flats and studios, for example, gives new life to a building while keeping the character of the district.

entries.label_vi: Bảo tàng miễn phí: mở rộng tiếp cận, giáo dục, người thu nhập thấp, nhiều khách hơn; nhưng cần kinh phí; có thể miễn cho dân địa phương, trẻ em
entries.claim: Free entry makes museums open to everyone, not only those who can afford a ticket.
entries.because: Families on low incomes, students and older people visit more often when no fee is charged, schools can bring classes without cost, and the knowledge held in public collections belongs to the public.
entries.result: Funding must be found elsewhere, through taxes, donations and shops, or by charging only for special exhibitions.
entries.reuse_vi: Đề bảo tàng miễn phí / thu phí.

entries.label_vi: Thu phí vào bảo tàng: nguồn thu, chất lượng; nhưng loại trừ người nghèo, giảm khách, có nguồn khác (thuế, tài trợ, cửa hàng, triển lãm đặc biệt)
entries.claim: Charging for entry raises money but excludes people and may reduce visitor numbers.
entries.because: Fees can pay for conservation and staff, yet they discourage low-income visitors, and museums have other sources of income such as grants, sponsors, shops and charges for special exhibitions.
entries.result: A mixed model keeps access wide while sharing the cost.
entries.reuse_vi: Đề bảo tàng thu phí.

entries.label_vi: Bảo tàng tập trung lịch sử địa phương: liên quan, bản sắc, tự hào cộng đồng, nhưng cần bối cảnh thế giới, cân bằng
entries.claim: Local history gives museums relevance, but a purely local focus can narrow understanding.
entries.because: People connect strongly with stories about their own town, family and neighbours, and local collections are often neglected elsewhere, yet visitors also need to see how local events fit into national and world history.
entries.result: A balance of local and wider themes serves visitors best.
entries.reuse_vi: Đề bảo tàng và lịch sử địa phương.

entries.label_vi: Bảo tàng trưng bày hiện vật nước khác: hiểu biết liên văn hoá, nhiều người xem; nhưng cướp bóc thời thuộc địa, yêu cầu hồi hương
entries.claim: Displaying artefacts from other countries widens understanding, but how they were acquired matters.
entries.because: National museums let visitors compare cultures and see objects that they could never travel to see, yet many items were taken during colonial rule or without consent, so countries of origin ask for their return.
entries.result: Items acquired legitimately may remain on show, while stolen ones should be returned or shared on loan.
entries.reuse_vi: Đề bảo tàng trưng bày hiện vật nước ngoài.

entries.label_vi: Phòng tranh 'tinh hoa'? Rào cản: giá, ngôn ngữ chuyên môn, cảm giác không thuộc; nhưng nhiều nơi miễn phí, hoạt động tiếp cận, nghệ thuật đa dạng
entries.claim: Galleries can feel exclusive, but many are working to open their doors.
entries.because: High prices, specialist language and an intimidating atmosphere can discourage newcomers, yet many galleries are free, offer family days and guided tours, and show art that reflects a wide range of communities.
entries.result: Elitism is a problem of habit and perception that can be changed.
entries.reuse_vi: Đề phòng tranh tinh hoa.

entries.label_vi: Nghệ thuật công cộng cải thiện thành phố: vẻ đẹp, bản sắc, gắn kết, du lịch; chi phí, thị hiếu, phá hoại
entries.claim: Public art makes shared spaces more attractive and gives a city a distinct character.
entries.because: Sculptures, murals and installations turn ordinary streets into places that people enjoy and remember, bring communities together and attract visitors, although they cost money and tastes differ.
entries.result: Involving residents in choosing and creating works reduces conflict.
entries.reuse_vi: Đề nghệ thuật công cộng.

entries.label_vi: Đài tưởng niệm gây tranh cãi: giữ lại để học lịch sử, có bối cảnh; một số tôn vinh tội ác có thể bị di dời; đối thoại
entries.claim: Controversial monuments can be kept if their history is explained.
entries.because: Removing them can hide uncomfortable parts of the past, whereas plaques, museums and discussion help people to learn, although some monuments honour people responsible for great harm and cause real pain to groups.
entries.result: Decisions should involve the affected community and clear criteria.
entries.reuse_vi: Đề đài tưởng niệm gây tranh cãi.

entries.label_vi: Dạy lịch sử nhiều góc nhìn: tư duy phản biện, công bằng, hiểu người khác; rủi ro: rối, thiếu thống nhất; cần bằng chứng
entries.claim: Teaching history from several perspectives builds critical thinking and fairness.
entries.because: Events look different to winners and losers, rulers and ordinary people, and comparing accounts teaches pupils to weigh evidence and to understand why people disagree, although too many versions without a clear framework may confuse.
entries.result: Students become better citizens and more careful readers.
entries.reuse_vi: Đề dạy lịch sử.

entries.label_vi: Thủ công truyền thống bảo tồn di sản: kỹ năng, bản sắc, sinh kế, du lịch; bị đe doạ bởi sản xuất hàng loạt
entries.claim: Traditional crafts keep skills, stories and identity alive.
entries.because: Techniques passed from master to apprentice carry knowledge of materials and designs developed over centuries, give communities a livelihood and attract tourists, but mass-produced goods threaten their survival.
entries.result: Support, training and fair prices help crafts to continue.
entries.reuse_vi: Đề thủ công truyền thống.

entries.label_vi: Chiếm dụng văn hoá: có hại khi lợi dụng, rập khuôn, không ghi nhận; nhưng trao đổi văn hoá là bình thường; phân biệt tôn trọng
entries.claim: Cultural appropriation is harmful when it exploits or mocks, but cultural exchange itself is natural.
entries.because: Companies that profit from sacred symbols without credit or payment, or costumes that reduce a culture to a stereotype, cause offence, whereas learning from and honouring another culture with permission enriches both sides.
entries.result: Respect, credit and fair sharing of benefits matter more than blanket bans.
entries.reuse_vi: Đề chiếm dụng văn hoá.

entries.text: A family with three children who would never pay for tickets, for example, may visit a free museum every month.
A student who cannot afford a twenty-pound ticket, for example, may never see a collection that is meant to belong to everyone.
A museum about the town's old textile mill, for example, helps residents to understand where their grandparents worked.
A statue removed from a temple without permission, for example, may be returned or shared on loan after discussions between the museum and the country of origin.
A first-time visitor who joins a free guided tour, for example, may find that a gallery is much friendlier than she expected.
A blank wall that is turned into a colourful mural, for example, can lift the mood of a whole street.
A statue of a controversial figure that carries a plaque explaining his crimes, for example, teaches visitors more than an empty plinth.
A class that reads accounts of the same battle from both armies, for example, learns that history depends on who is telling it.
A young weaver who learns patterns from an elder, for example, keeps alive a technique that no book could fully record.
A fashion brand that copies a sacred pattern from an indigenous community without permission, for example, profits from a tradition that its owners cannot protect.

entries.label_vi: Lễ kỷ niệm công cộng tốn tiền, thức ăn, năng lượng, rác, ồn; nhưng đem lại gắn kết, du lịch, văn hoá; có thể tổ chức tiết kiệm
entries.claim: Public celebrations cost money and create waste, but they also bring lasting benefits.
entries.because: Fireworks, decorations and security cost large sums and leave litter, yet they strengthen community spirit, attract visitors and mark shared history, and costs can be reduced through sensible planning and sponsorship.
entries.result: Celebrations are worthwhile when they are well managed.
entries.reuse_vi: Đề lễ kỷ niệm công cộng lãng phí.

entries.label_vi: Sự kiện gia đình riêng: thân mật, cá nhân, rẻ, kiểm soát; nhưng ít kết nối cộng đồng
entries.claim: Private family events are intimate, personal and easier to control.
entries.because: Small gatherings let relatives and close friends talk properly, follow their own customs and spend according to their means, whereas public celebrations are crowded, noisy and expensive for the organisers.
entries.result: Both kinds of celebration meet different needs.
entries.reuse_vi: Đề lễ hội công cộng vs sự kiện gia đình.

entries.label_vi: Lễ hội văn hoá hỗ trợ kinh tế địa phương: chi tiêu của khách, việc làm tạm thời, quảng bá, hàng thủ công, ngoài mùa; nhưng tạm thời, chi phí
entries.claim: Cultural festivals bring money, jobs and publicity to the places that host them.
entries.because: Visitors spend on food, accommodation and souvenirs, stalls and performers earn income, and media coverage promotes the area, though much of the work is temporary.
entries.result: Local businesses gain most when residents are involved in organising and supplying the event.
entries.reuse_vi: Đề lễ hội văn hoá và kinh tế địa phương.

entries.label_vi: Thời trang định hình bản sắc văn hoá: thể hiện cá nhân, thuộc nhóm, trang phục truyền thống quốc gia, địa vị; nhưng áp lực thương mại, đồng phục hoá
entries.claim: Clothing communicates who people are and where they belong.
entries.because: Traditional dress expresses national and regional heritage, personal style shows individuality and group membership, and festivals and ceremonies keep customs visible, although global brands push everyone towards similar looks.
entries.result: Fashion both reflects and shapes cultural identity.
entries.reuse_vi: Đề thời trang và bản sắc.

entries.label_vi: Streaming nhạc: người nghe có kho nhạc, rẻ, dễ khám phá; nghệ sĩ thu nhập thấp, bài ngắn, mất giá trị album; nên cải cách chia tiền
entries.claim: Streaming has made music cheap and easy to find for listeners but has hurt many artists' incomes.
entries.because: Millions of songs are available for a monthly fee and new artists can reach a global audience, yet each stream pays only a tiny amount, so musicians who are not already famous earn little and albums have lost importance.
entries.result: Fairer payment systems and live work are needed to keep musicians in business.
entries.reuse_vi: Đề streaming nhạc.

entries.label_vi: Nhạc sống: không khí, trải nghiệm chung, chân thực, ủng hộ nghệ sĩ; đắt, đông, âm thanh. Nhạc thu sẵn: tiện, rẻ, chất lượng ổn, nhiều lựa chọn
entries.claim: Live concerts offer atmosphere and shared experience, while recorded music offers convenience and choice.
entries.because: At a concert fans feel energy and share emotion with thousands, and artists earn directly, but tickets are expensive and crowds tiring, whereas recordings can be enjoyed anywhere, at any time, for little money.
entries.result: Most people enjoy both at different moments.
entries.reuse_vi: Đề nhạc sống vs nhạc thu.

entries.label_vi: Nghe nhạc giúp tập trung: với việc lặp lại, chặn tiếng ồn, cải thiện tâm trạng; lời bài hát làm xao nhãng việc phức tạp; khác nhau theo cá nhân
entries.claim: Music can help concentration on simple or repetitive tasks but may distract from demanding ones.
entries.because: Calm, familiar music blocks noise and improves mood, which helps with routine work, yet songs with lyrics compete with reading and writing, and people differ in how they respond.
entries.result: The benefit depends on the task and the type of music.
entries.reuse_vi: Đề nghe nhạc và tập trung.

entries.label_vi: Đọc tiểu thuyết tăng đồng cảm: sống trong tâm trí người khác, hiểu động cơ, góc nhìn khác; nghiên cứu ủng hộ; không đảm bảo
entries.claim: Reading fiction lets people live inside other minds and so strengthens empathy.
entries.because: Novels invite readers to share the thoughts and feelings of characters from different backgrounds, which trains the habit of seeing situations from another point of view, although the effect depends on how the reader engages.
entries.result: Readers of fiction often score higher on tests of understanding others.
entries.reuse_vi: Đề tiểu thuyết và đồng cảm.

entries.label_vi: Học ngôn ngữ cải thiện hiểu biết văn hoá: thành ngữ, cách nghĩ, tiếp cận văn học, giao tiếp trực tiếp; cần học cả văn hoá
entries.claim: Learning a language gives direct access to another way of thinking and living.
entries.because: Idioms, humour and forms of politeness reveal values that translations lose, learners can read literature and talk to people in their own words, and effort to communicate earns respect.
entries.result: Language study works best when culture is learned alongside grammar.
entries.reuse_vi: Đề học ngôn ngữ và hiểu biết văn hoá.

entries.label_vi: Biển báo song ngữ: giúp du khách, người nhập cư, an toàn, tôn trọng ngôn ngữ thiểu số; chi phí, rối mắt
entries.claim: Bilingual signs help visitors and residents to find their way and feel respected.
entries.because: Tourists, newcomers and speakers of minority languages can understand directions, warnings and services, which improves safety and access, though extra text costs money and can clutter signs.
entries.result: Careful design and the use of symbols reduce the drawbacks.
entries.reuse_vi: Đề biển báo song ngữ.

entries.text: A town that spends a large sum on fireworks, for example, may see them last for twenty minutes, but residents remember the evening for years.
A birthday dinner with ten relatives, for example, lets everyone talk and share stories, which is difficult in a crowd of thousands.
A potter who sells her work at a festival stall, for example, may earn in a weekend what she usually earns in a month.
A young woman who wears her grandmother's traditional dress to a festival, for example, shows pride in her heritage and starts conversations about its meaning.
A musician whose song is played a million times, for example, may earn only a few thousand pounds, which would not cover the cost of making an album.
A fan who sings along with ten thousand strangers, for example, enjoys a feeling of togetherness that headphones cannot provide.
A student who listens to quiet instrumental music while tidying notes, for example, may work faster, but the same student may find lyrics distracting during an essay.
A reader who follows a refugee's journey in a novel, for example, may understand fear and hope in a way that a news report does not convey.
A learner who discovers that a polite phrase in another language has no direct translation, for example, begins to see how manners differ between cultures.
A railway station with signs in two languages, for example, helps a traveller to find the right platform without asking for help.
National days, cultural festivals and anniversary parades
